pass_a_gloss: [continuing: 'these the angels who in night'] guard us. Chapter 38, verse 5. Who set its measures, if you know? or who is the one who brought a cord (line) upon it? The Greeks wished to say something about the measure of the earth: the diameter of the earth, they say, [is] stades of twenty-five myriads (250,000). But the word (passage) seems to show that the measure of the earth is ungraspable to everyone; only the Saviour knows it, who is also creator. And measures, and not measure, he said, so that he might present the differences of the earth. What is the measure of such and such, let us say, of the East bearing the spices? measure of the [land] bearing the pepper or the animals? for not all things come to be everywhere; these measures then are with the Word of God. So not simply was the earth made so great, nor as it chanced, but it seems to me, if even the chance (least) thing were added, it would be untimely (out of place), and if it were taken away, by the like reason it would ruin all of it; and this the measures and the cord hint at. Verse 6 (numeral lost). And who is the one who threw a corner stone upon it? Who is the one who threw a corner stone upon it, that thus it stands seated (firm), as though he built upon a secured footing of foundation? by the will of God, for in his hand all the ends of the earth. Corner stone: this can also be understood toward the Only-begotten Son of God, for us made flesh; according to the [word] in psalms: Stone which they rejected, it became for head of corner. For by good-pleasure of the Father having come upon earth, he joined in himself the two peoples, of Jews and of nations, just as indeed also the corner stone binds both walls. Verse 11. And I said to it: Up to this you will come, and you will not pass over. Symmachus: Until here let the lifting (swell) of your waves be set. For thus securely he holds it as though with bars; and thus easily, as though in order (by arrangement). For I said, he says, and there is no speaking against, when, no necessity pushing, this happens; at once although much force and strength whip it; for because of this he did not let it be calm, nor tame, so that it may proclaim the strength of God, the nature fighting the command, and the command everywhere conquering. For if the water were tame, many would have reckoned the good order to the nature of the water; but now being troubled, being whipped, being pushed inside, and not able to overstep the bounds, through the trouble it proclaims the strength of God. Verse 41. And who prepared food for a raven? For it is said not to rear the young; but they themselves fittingly, being big, procure food. But the young who rears? not the word of God? as also the gospel says: The birds of the heaven do not sow nor reap, and your heavenly father feeds them. Chapter 39, verse 27. And at your command is the eagle raised? and a vulture on its nest having sat, does it lodge on a projection of rock and hidden [place]? [dots: text missing] If among the flesh-eaters some rational wisdom, from the knowledge according to nature being in each, and toward knowledge, to the one of war, to the others of those who have died, you see also one air-borne, the vulture. Verse 34 (catena numbering; English 40:4). Why am I still judged, being admonished and reproving the Lord, hearing such things, being nothing? Why still, he says, am I judged, for a preface? and from the beginning he yielded the first places. I have been defeated, he says, with you in the just claim; why further do you prosecute the case? for what is it possible to answer? and how must one look in the face toward such a master? I, he says, continued seeking the cause of the blow that came upon me; but against the creation (workmanship) I charged nothing, and toward the things said I have nothing to say. It is lacking (an ellipsis): as not even reproving the Lord, being admonished, the wretched one. Chapter 40, verse 2 (catena; English 40:7). But gird, like a man, your loin, and I will ask you, and you answer me. For those trusting in abundance of just claims, not even fleeing (shunning) the opponents, let go (give leave), so that out of abundance the victory comes. Then he also defends himself to him, that I care about men; clear from there, for what reason I brought this trial upon you. I give you boldness, I will ask you, and you answer me. Verse 3 (catena; English 40:8). Do you think that I have dealt (given oracle) to you otherwise, than that you might appear just? He says the present oracle (divine answer); not so that I condemn, I say these things, he says, but so that I show just. Or about the trial he says, calling the permission an oracle, that is, that I ordered beforehand that this happen for some other reason; he did not say, so that you become, but so that you appear what you were, so that you may teach the others. But see: he did not say, so that you become just (for which righteousness exactly [continues in the next unit: 'you practised'])
pass_b_english: “Who fixed its measures, if you know? Or who is it that stretched a line over it?” (Job 38:5). The Greeks did want to say something about the measure of the earth: the diameter of the earth, they say, is twenty-five myriads of stades. But the passage seems to show that the measure of the earth is beyond everyone's grasp; only the Saviour knows it, who is also the Creator. He said “measures,” and not “measure,” to set before us the differences in the earth. What is the measure of this or that land: of the East, say, which bears the spices? What is the measure of the land that bears pepper, or the animals? For not everything grows everywhere. These measures, then, are with the Word of God. So the earth has not come to be of this size without reason, nor by chance; it seems to me that if even the slightest thing were added, it would be out of place, and if anything were taken away, by the same reasoning it would spoil the whole earth. This is what the measures and the line hint at.

“And who is it that laid a cornerstone upon it?” (Job 38:6). Who is it that laid a cornerstone upon it, so that it stands so firmly fixed, as though built upon the secure footing of a foundation? By the will of God, for in his hand are all the ends of the earth (Psalm 95:4). “A cornerstone”: this can also be understood of the only-begotten Son of God, made flesh for our sake, according to the word in the Psalms: “The stone which they rejected has become the head of the corner” (Psalm 118:22). For coming to earth by the good pleasure of the Father, he joined in himself the two peoples, the Jews and the Gentiles, just as, of course, the cornerstone binds both walls together.

“And I said to it, ‘Thus far you shall come, and you shall not pass beyond’” (Job 38:11). Symmachus: “Up to here let the swelling of your waves be set.” So securely does he hold it in, as if with bars; and so easily, as if by a set order. For “I said,” he says, and there is no answering back, when this comes about with no constraint driving it, and that although great force and strength are lashing the sea. This is why he did not let it be calm or gentle: so that it might proclaim God's strength, its nature fighting against the command and the command everywhere prevailing. If the water were gentle, many would have credited its good order to the nature of water. But as it is, troubled, lashed, driven back within, and unable to pass its bounds, by its very turmoil it proclaims the strength of God.

“And who prepared food for the raven?” (Job 38:41). For it is said not to rear its young. The grown birds, naturally, being large, find food for themselves; but who rears the young? Is it not the word of God? As the Gospel too says: “The birds of the heaven do not sow, nor do they reap, and your heavenly Father feeds them” (Matthew 6:26).

“Is it at your command that the eagle mounts up, and the vulture, having settled on its nest, lodges on a jutting rock and in a hidden place?” (Job 39:27-28). … If among the flesh-eaters there is some reasoning wisdom, present in each from the knowledge it has by nature, and directed to knowing, for one of them war, for others the dead, you see it in the vulture too, a single bird borne through the air.

“Why am I still judged, being admonished and reproving the Lord, when I hear such things, I who am nothing?” (Job 40:4). “Why am I still judged?” he says, by way of a preface; and from the start he gave up the first place. I am beaten in my case before you, he says; why do you press the suit further? For what answer can be given? And how should one look such a master in the face? I, he says, kept on seeking the cause of the blow that fell on me; but I brought no charge against the work of creation, and I have nothing to say against what has been said. Something is left unsaid: as one not even reproving the Lord, the wretched man being admonished.

“But gird your loins like a man; I will ask you, and you answer me” (Job 40:7). For those who are confident in an abundance of just claims do not even shun their opponents but give them leave, so that the victory may come out of that abundance. Then he also makes his defence to him: I care about human beings; it is plain from this why I brought this trial upon you. I give you freedom to speak: I will ask you, and you answer me.

“Do you think that I have dealt with you for any other reason than that you might be shown to be righteous?” (Job 40:8). He means the present divine answer: I do not say these things to condemn you, he says, but to show you righteous. Or he is speaking of the trial, calling the permission a divine dealing, that is: that I had ordained this to happen for some other reason. He did not say, “that you might become,” but, “that you might appear as what you were,” so that you might teach the others. choices.choice: Old English paraphrased, inverted and misread many clauses and gave wrong labels ('Ch. 40, 5' for 38:5, '(14)' for 38:11, 'Ch. 28, 27' for 38:41 and 39:27, 'Ch. 24' for 40:4, 'Ch. 4, 4' for 40:7). Retranslated clause by clause; each lemma opens a paragraph with its verse.

'To live as a man by your strength' replaced: ζῶσαι = gird (not ζῆσαι). 'claiming that men do not concern him' replaced: ὅτι μέλει μοι περὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων = I care about human beings (negation reversed in the old text). 'struggling against the laws of nature by His command' replaced: τῆς φύσεως τῷ προστάγματι μαχομένης = its nature fighting against the command. 'calls forgiveness a profit' replaced: χρηματισμὸν τὴν συγχώρησιν = calls the permission a divine dealing. 'he summoned no one regarding the creation' replaced: εἰς δημιουργίαν οὐδὲν ἐνεκάλεσα = I brought no charge against the work of creation. 'having settled upon a carcass, cry out' replaced: the lemma is the vulture settling on its nest and lodging on a rock. 'became flesh through us' replaced: δι' ἡμᾶς = for our sake. 'the Word reveals' replaced: ὁ λόγος here is the passage. 'fragrances ... spices' replaced: ἀρώματα = spices, πέπερ = pepper.
Old 'The Ally replied' was Ὁ δὲ Σύμμαχος misread; now 'Symmachus: …'.
The Greek quotes 'Λίθον, ὃν ἀπεδοκίμασαν' without 'the builders'; rendered as given, 'The stone which they rejected'.

Print marks a gap ('.....') and the Εἰ clause has no verb (σοφίαν accusative). Rendered closely with '… [a gap in the text]' and 'there is' supplied; 'for one of them war, for others the dead' keeps τῷ μὲν πολέμου, τοῖς δὲ τῶν ἀποθανόντων. A human should check this sentence against another witness if one is found.
Grammatical note that something is to be understood; rendered 'Something is left unsaid:' followed by the catena's words as given.

choices.issue: οὐδὲ φεύγοντες τοὺς ἀντιδίκους, ἀφίασιν (40:7 note)
choices.choice: φεύγω + accusative taken as 'shun'; ἀφίασιν without object rendered 'give them leave'. A legal sense (φεύγοντες = defendants) is possible; the chosen sense fits the next line 'I give you freedom to speak'.
Lost stigma before Τίς δέ ἐστιν ὁ βαλὼν λίθον γωνιαῖον restored as ϛʹ = 38:6; page numbers 384-386 (386 printed twice) dropped; 'Αρα' read as ἄρα ('so').

The catena numbers 'Why am I still judged' as ΛΘ λδʹ (39:34) and the next lemmas as Μʹ βʹ, γʹ (40:2, 40:3); in English Bibles these are Job 40:4, 40:7 and 40:8, which are cited (English numbering, as the morning log did for Job 41).

Section ends mid-sentence ('ἣν γὰρ ἀκριβῶς τὴν δικαιοσύνην', completed by 'ἤσκησας' at the start of u03-open); rendered '(for the righteousness which with exactness you …'; u03-open begins '… practised)', so the clause joins across the break.
'joined in himself the two peoples' echoes Ephesians 2:14-15; recorded in added_allusions, not printed in the text, since it is an allusion and not a quotation.
Review 2026-11-11: '[a gap in the text]' removed from the reading text; the edition's '.....' is shown by the ellipsis and recorded here.
